## The problem

Our team of twelve has drifted into long-lived feature branches, some open for three or four weeks before merging. Merges have become dreaded events: conflicts pile up, integration bugs surface late, and reviewers face sprawling diffs that are hard to reason about. Last sprint we lost two full days resolving conflicts on the payments branch, and a regression shipped because two branches had touched the same configuration in incompatible ways without either author knowing. The longer a branch lives, the more it diverges from main, and the more expensive and risky reconciliation becomes.

- Average branch lifetime has grown from roughly 3 days to 18 days over the past two quarters
- Three production incidents this quarter trace directly to merge conflicts or integration issues discovered only at merge time

## The proposal

I propose we move to trunk-based development: everyone commits small, frequent changes directly to main (or through branches that live less than a day), guarded by feature flags for anything incomplete. This shrinks the size of any single integration, surfaces conflicts while they're still cheap to fix, and keeps main always releasable.

- Adopt feature flags for in-progress work so incomplete features never block a release
- Require CI to pass on every merge to main, with a strict "fix it or revert it" rule for breakages
- Set a team norm of merging at least once per day per active task, paired with lightweight, same-day code review

## What could go wrong

The strongest objection is that our test suite isn't fast or reliable enough to support constant merging to main; a flaky or slow pipeline could turn "merge daily" into "break main daily," and a broken main blocks everyone, not just one branch's owner. This is a real risk, not a hypothetical one — our CI already takes 25 minutes and fails intermittently. Trunk-based development amplifies the cost of any test-suite weakness we currently paper over by isolating work in branches. Before rolling this out broadly, we should invest a sprint in stabilizing and speeding up CI, and pilot the workflow with one squad first to validate that main stays green in practice. If we can't get CI reliable, we should delay rather than force the switch.

I would like a decision by the end of next week.
